name: Jira
tagline: Issue tracking and project workflows through Atlassian APIs.
shortDescription: Jira Cloud exposes REST APIs, OAuth, Forge/Connect apps, webhooks, JQL, issues, projects, and workflows.
agentSummary: Agents can automate Jira through REST APIs and Atlassian's Rovo MCP server for Jira, Confluence, and Compass search, summaries, issue creation, and updates.
bestFor: Issue triage, sprint hygiene, workflow updates, and project operations.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Workflow transitions, permissions, and customer data need review. Project, CRM, document, and spreadsheet writes depend on team context and privacy rules; require least-privilege scopes and review for workflow-changing actions. MCP servers inherit the connected account's scopes and may send prompts or data to third-party services; configure read-only or narrow scopes when available. API automation needs client-side throttling, idempotency where supported, pagination limits, retries, and audit logging.
pricingSummary: Public Atlassian plan pricing with free and paid tiers.
authModel: Atlassian API tokens, OAuth apps, user permissions, and Atlassian Rovo MCP OAuth/API-token access.
browserSupport: Browser UI is useful for workflow, board, and permission review.

capabilities.detail: Jira Cloud REST API covers issues, projects, fields, transitions, and search.
Atlassian Rovo MCP Server connects AI clients to Jira, Confluence, and Compass through OAuth 2.1 and existing user permissions.
Atlassian developer docs include REST, Forge, OAuth, and webhooks.
Jira pricing is public by plan and user count.
Browser UI is useful for workflow, board, and permission review.
